answer: A work-staked reputation ledger resists sybils: each agent earns a pearl of trust only after completing verifiable jobs whose results peers can check, and pearls decay over time. Spinning up thousands of fake identities buys nothing, because trust accrues slowly per identity and each job costs real compute plus a refundable bond slashed on fraud. An oasis of newcomers can still join, but they start untrusted and must prove themselves before touching shared funds. Raising the horizon of required history makes mass fakery expensive while honest agents compound.
